The TImmLeaf defs, the builtin patterns (int_riscv_pulp_bclr/bset/binsert :1907/:1911), the clip/extract/insert patterns, the register-form bclr/bset patterns and P_EXTHZ/P_EXTBZ are unchanged. review_notes.isa_semantics: Checked in GVSoC gvsoc2/core/models/cpu/iss/include/isa/pulp_v2.hpp:1967 p_bclri_exec and :2041 p_bseti_exec: width = UIM0+1, shift = UIM1, mask = ((1<<width)-1)<<shift. isa_lib/int.h: lib_BCLR = val & ~mask and lib_BSET = val | mask. The encoding in isa_gen/isa_pulpv2.py:496-497 is 11|Is3[29:25]|Is2[24:20]|rs1|011 or 100|rd|0110011. The worker's example word ce853533 decodes to p.bclr a0,a0,7,8.
review_notes.predicate_exactness: Imm is the sign-extended i32. isShiftedMask_32 truncates to 32 bits, so the ~Imm of a sign-extended value is handled correctly. isInt<12>(Imm) on the sign-extended value is exactly upstream Zbs BCLRMask/SingleBitSetMask (RISCVInstrInfoZb.td:61-72 at llvmorg-20.1.8, verified). The XForms use countl/countr_{one,zero}<uint32_t>, so there are no 64-bit popcount artifacts. Width 32 cannot be reached: and 0 and or -1 fit andi/ori and are excluded, and and -1 is not a shifted mask. 0xffff is excluded only for and (p.exthz). The pattern predicates [IsRV32, HasPULPExtV2] match the TTI gate (hasPULPExtV2 && !is64Bit && 32-bit).
review_notes.my_gvsoc_test: Independent generator in scratchpad/rv/gen.py. It covers every contiguous field (all 528 width/offset pairs, width 1..32, offsets 0..32-w) as both and ~field and or field, alternating unsigned hex literals and signed negative decimal literals. It adds 40 xor controls, 60 random non-contiguous and/or masks and explicit edges: 0, -1, 0xffff, 0xff, 0x7ff, -2048, 0xfffff7ff, 0x800, 0xfff, 0xfffff000, 0x80000000, 0x7fffffff, 0xffff0000. It also has 24 multi-use functions (constant hoisting) and 24 volatile RMW loops, 1184+48 functions in all. The reference is computed on target from a volatile-loaded mask with plain and/or/xor. The GVSoC ri5ky_testbench gives 16376 checks and 0 mismatches at -O2, -Os and -O3 with -verify-machineinstrs; int-20 also gives 0. Selection audit on -O2 asm: all 913 masks expected to select (contiguous, not int12, not and-0xffff) are exactly `p.b{clr,set} a0,a0,w-1,off; ret`. Nothing else uses p.bclr/p.bset, xor never does, int12 masks stay andi/ori and and 0xffff stays p.exthz. Edges: x&0x7fffffff -> p.bclr 0,31; x|0x80000000 -> p.bset 0,31; x&0x80000000 -> p.bclr 30,0; x|0x7fffffff -> p.bset 30,0; x|-4096 -> p.bset 19,12; x&4095 -> p.bclr 19,12; x|4095 -> p.bset 11,0; x&-4096 -> p.bclr 11,0. bits.o is 3245 instructions against 4984 for int-20.
review_notes.tti_change: Correct and safe. It says the mask is free exactly when the new ImmLeaf would select a single instruction (p.bclr/p.bset), or when the constant was already free (int12) or is and 0xffff (single p.exthz). So hoisting never leaves a constant that then needs materialising. xor is excluded, and the change is gated on the same subtarget feature and XLen as the patterns. Verified with opt -passes=consthoist: -65281 (and) and 0x0ffffff0 (or) are not hoisted with +xpulpv, they are hoisted without it, and the xor with the same constant is still hoisted with +xpulpv. SDK sample: 100 random strict-compilable TUs with this build against the int20-snap clang (d17dc7f4f2f9, integration head plus two unrelated fixups). 6 objects changed and all shrank: 37374 -> 37355 instructions (pk.c, bignum_core.c, event_groups.c, bignum.c, psa_crypto_cipher.c, psa_crypto_aead.c). In bignum_core.c the only change is 0xffff no longer being hoisted: p.exthz replaces and-with-register, which frees a register and removes spills. event_groups.c gets slli/srli -> p.bclr 7,24 and lui+or -> p.bset 0,25. The GAP9 sweep: the worker's official_sweep_compare.txt reports 54/54 identical, which is plausible because the kernels use no wide masks; I did not rerun it. Decision: keep it. It is the same root cause (p.bclr/p.bset unreachable from plain C), and upstream pairs its Zbs bclri/bseti patterns with the same getIntImmCostInst entries (RISCVTargetTransformInfo.cpp:212/:225 at llvmorg-20.1.8, verified). It is a separate commit in a file the fork already touches, so it can still be dropped on its own.
